title: Conservation of Momentum in Collisions
learning_goal: Analyze conservation of momentum in one-dimensional elastic and inelastic collisions.

stages.title: 1. Total momentum is conserved
stages.content: In an isolated system, total momentum before a collision equals total momentum after the collision. Keep a consistent positive direction when assigning signs to velocity.

stages.title: 2. Elastic collisions
stages.content: In an elastic collision, total momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved.

stages.title: 3. Inelastic collisions
stages.content: In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not. In a perfectly inelastic collision, the objects stick together after impact.

stages.title: 4. Worked example
stages.content: A 2 kg cart moving at 4 m/s strikes a 2 kg cart at rest and they stick together. Initial momentum is 8 kg·m/s. The combined mass is 4 kg, so the final velocity is 8/4 = 2 m/s.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: A 3 kg cart moving at 4 m/s collides with a 1 kg cart at rest. They stick together. What is their final velocity?
stages.hint: Find total momentum before the collision, then divide by the combined mass.
stages.alternate_explanation: Because they stick together, treat the two carts as one combined object after the collision.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, apply conservation of momentum in one dimension, distinguish elastic from inelastic collisions, use signs consistently, and solve perfectly inelastic collision problems.

concept_cards.title: When is total momentum conserved for a colliding system?
concept_cards.content: Internal interaction forces cancel in the system momentum balance. External impulse, not the collision label alone, determines momentum conservation.

concept_cards.title: Two carts stick together after impact. What kind of collision is this?
concept_cards.content: Sticking defines a perfectly inelastic collision. Momentum can be conserved while kinetic energy decreases into deformation, thermal energy, or sound.
